note: Realistic animal models (Dave 6 Nov 2026: aim for photorealism; design/realistic_animals_plan.md, src/client/animal_view.gd _make_model). A species row here whose scene exists is drawn from that rigged, animated scene instead of the code-built body; no row or a missing file keeps the code body. Row: scene (res:// path of a .glb/.fbx/.tscn), scale, yaw_deg (turn so the animal faces -Z), walk_mps and run_mps (ground speeds the walk and run clips were made at), stride_m (metres per footstep), clips {state number or 'walk'/'run': clip name}; states 0 graze, 1 hop, 2 flee, 3 alert, 10 warn, 11 charge, 12 recover. Example: "bear": {"scene": "res://assets/animals/bear/bear.glb", "scale": 1.0, "yaw_deg": 180, "walk_mps": 1.3, "run_mps": 9.0, "stride_m": 1.1, "clips": {"0": "Eat", "3": "Idle", "10": "Roar", "11": "Run", "12": "Idle", "walk": "Walk", "run": "Run"}}. clip_prefix is put before every clip name (WildMesh: the armature, e.g. 'RigRoot|'). The model files are bought (WildMesh 3D Ultimate 3D Animal Pack, Dave 6 Nov 2026) and are NOT in git (/assets/animals/ is ignored): copy them from the pack into assets/animals/<kind>/ on a build machine.

bear.note: WildMesh BrownBear (Realistic Animals/BrownBear/SK_Bear.fbx, textures in its Textures folder): 7508 triangles, 35 bones, 81 clips; faces +Z, so yaw 180. Alert stands up on its hind legs; warn is the angry breathing stance; charge sprints.
